column7: The card is part of the current document and is styled with it, so div groups it; iframe would load a separate document with its own browsing context, which this content is not.

The booking page is a separate document whose styles must stay apart, so iframe embeds it in its own browsing context; div cannot hold another document. It needs no device feature, so no allow permission should be granted.

The article is a separate document but must share styles and the accessibility tree. An iframe isolates it, a div on the page integrates its copied markup; neither alone meets both wishes, so the answer depends on whether integration or isolation matters more.
The call page is a separate, isolated document, so iframe; it needs the camera, so allow should list exactly that requested feature and nothing more.
It is not stated whether the help content is a separate HTML document or markup of this page, and that decides between div and iframe; the right move is to ask.
The steps must be done in order, and ol is for items whose order matters.
The ingredients can be gathered in any order, and ul is for items whose order does not matter.
The position of each book is its rank, so the order carries meaning and ol fits.
The footer links have no meaningful order, so ul fits.
Nothing says whether the order of the party items matters, which is exactly what separates ol from ul; the right move is to ask.
A tiny script used on one page with no CSP and no ordering need works either inline or as an external file; reuse and caching would favour external but neither applies.
The same code is needed on every page, and an external file can be cached and reused while inline code is repeated in every page.

The policy lacks unsafe-inline, which blocks inline script code, while external scripts from allowed sources still run; script-src 'self' allows the site's own files and files can be added, so moving the code to an external file on the same origin keeps the page working.

The policy ('self' without unsafe-inline) blocks plain inline code and no file can be added, so the only option is an inline block allowed by a nonce or hash, which holds only if the policy can be given that nonce or hash.
defer runs an external classic script after parsing in document order; on an inline classic script defer is ignored, and the code is not a module.
defer is ignored on an inline classic script and no file can be added, so the code can only be delayed by making it an inline module, which holds only if the classic code works unchanged as a module.
Module scripts are already deferred by default, so defer is not needed and has no effect; the code imports modules, so it must be loaded as a module.
